title: Submission to God-Given Authority
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Submission to God-given authority means recognizing that authority exists under God and must be honored according to His Word. No human authority is absolute, and authority must never be used as permission for pride, oppression, or sin.
summary: Submission to God-given authority means recognizing that authority exists under God and must be honored according to His Word. No human authority is absolute, and authority must never be used as permission for pride, oppression, or sin.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the supreme Lord over every authority. He submitted without sin, confronted corrupt authority with truth, and now reigns over all powers as King.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture teaches that authority is not random. God orders human life with structures of authority in family, church, work, and government, and His people are called to honor Him in how they respond.

Submission is never worship of authority. Human authorities remain accountable to God. When commanded to sin, believers must obey God rather than men.

Authority must also be exercised under God. Leaders, parents, employers, and rulers are not free to oppress, abuse, exploit, or act as though people belong to them absolutely.

Christ’s lordship governs both those under authority and those who hold it. The believer’s obedience, courage, resistance, and service must all be shaped by His Word.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people reject all authority because authority has been abused. Others submit blindly and enable harm. Scripture gives a wiser path: honor authority under God while refusing sin and oppression.

This doctrine is especially important for protecting the vulnerable. Biblical submission must never be twisted into a tool for spiritual abuse, domestic harm, or silencing truth.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Honor God in how you respond to authority, but never treat human authority as higher than the Lord. If you hold authority, use it to serve, protect, and lead under Christ. If authority commands sin or enables harm, seek wisdom and obey God faithfully.
